title: KV cache: hotness-sampling and tiered reclaimer playbook
content:
Summary:
This doc proposes a pragmatic, low-risk design for an adaptive KV cache reclaimer that emphasizes: sampling-based hotness estimation, multi-tier memory pools (hot/warm/cold), background incremental compaction, and latency-aware eviction decisions. The goal is to reduce tail latency regressions caused by aggressive reclamation while addressing external fragmentation on long-lived servers.

Context / Motivation:
- Existing issues: increased OOM spikes during traffic spikes, unpredictable token-latency variance when large compactions run synchronously, and poor eviction choices when access patterns are bursty (hot items evicted, reloaded).
- Previous designs in this folder focus on slab buckets, buddy allocators, and proactive compaction. This doc intentionally explores a complementary approach centered on runtime hotness signals and a tiered reclaimer that demotes items before evicting them.

Goals (what success looks like):
- Reduce eviction-induced cache miss penalty by 30% for bursty workloads (measured as backend fetch rate after eviction).
- Keep 99th percentile token latency change due to cache maintenance < 5% vs baseline.
- Reduce external fragmentation metric (free-run fragmentation score, see metrics) by 25% over 7 days on mixed workloads.
- Operates under constrained CPU budget (max 2 vCPU dedicated to background compaction per GPU node).

Non-goals:
- This is NOT a replacement for a full slabless allocator; allocator internals remain orthogonal. We assume an allocator API that can: allocate(size, arena), free(ptr), iterate_free_runs(arena, callback), and optionally relocate(ptr, new_ptr).

High-level design:
1) Hotness sampling daemon: light-weight periodic sampling of accesses to estimate per-key hotness using reservoir sampling + exponential decay counters (low memory).
2) Tiered pools: each arena (NUMA/GPU-local) exposes three logical tiers: hot, warm, cold. Allocation prefers hot/warm tiers; cold is used for long tail items and is the primary candidate for compaction/eviction.
3) Demotion pipeline: rather than outright evict on first reclaim, items are demoted from hot->warm->cold based on hotness thresholds; cold items are eligible for relocation/eviction.
4) Background incremental compaction (reclaimer): runs in small time-sliced work units, coalesces adjacent free runs, and relocates small live objects into denser pages to reduce fragmentation. Compaction is rate-limited and SLO-aware.
5) Latency-aware eviction decision: eviction uses probabilistic choice between (A) local cold eviction, (B) remote model-serving fallback (if configured), and (C) async prefetch hints. The decision factors include hotness score, last-access delta, request SLO headroom, and current GPU load.

Data structures and APIs assumed:
- KVEntry metadata (kept in small header): key_hash, ptr, size_class, last_access_ts, hot_score_mod (8 bits), tier (2 bits).
- HotnessSketch: per-arena compact structure: N counters (N configurable) storing exponentially decayed counts. Updates are O(1) per access. We avoid a full LFU to limit memory.
- FreeRunIndex: free-run tree per arena to find best-fit candidates for coalescing and relocation.

Hotness sampling algorithm (rough):
- On every Nth access (configurable sampling_rate, default N=20), capture key_hash and increment a slot in HotnessSketch: slot = hash(key_hash) % NCOUNTERS; counters[slot] = alpha * counters[slot] + 1.
- Periodic decay tick (every T seconds): counters[i] *= decay_factor (alpha in 0.95..0.999 range depending on expected item lifetime).
- Hot score = counters[slot] scaled by recency weight derived from last_access_ts.
- Advantages: constant mem per arena, robust to bursty updates, and cheap updates inline with request handling when sampling hits.

Tier assignment and demotion policy:
- New allocations land in warm by default (optimistic). If sampling or access trace shows frequent hits (score > hot_threshold) within a short window, promote to hot.
- Demotion: sliding window check runs every epoch (default 30s). If hot_score < demote_threshold, move hot->warm; if warm score < demote2_threshold, move warm->cold.
- Movement is metadata-only (one atomic write) except when relocation is required for compaction.

Eviction strategy (tiered + sampling-aware):
- Primary candidates: cold tier contiguous runs, selected via FreeRunIndex. Eviction picks a run by weighted random sampling proportional to (fragmentation_score * size) to avoid always removing smallest objects.
- To prevent repeated churn of mildly-hot items, eviction probability for an item is: P_eviction = base_prob * exp(-beta * hot_score) where beta controls sensitivity. Items with recent accesses have near-zero probability.
- If eviction would cause a request to block on a backend fetch that exceeds configured per-request SLO, prefer to demote or spill-to-disk (if allowed) instead.
- When freeing space, best-effort relocation tries to pack small live objects into dedicated compaction pages; if relocation would take > max_reloc_time (configurable per work slice), abort and schedule next slice.

Compaction and relocation details:
- Compaction work units: the reclaimer takes a target free size budget per epoch (e.g., 64KiB per 100ms slice) and scans the FreeRunIndex for candidate holes adjacent to many small live objects.
- If allocator supports atomic relocate(src, dst): perform relocation under epoch-protected pointer updates; use read-copy-update for short window pointer swap to avoid blocking readers.
- If relocation requires copying large KV values, copy into an async buffer and update header only after a durability check to avoid double-free races.
- Background compaction prioritization: prioritize arenas with highest fragmentation_score * (1 + eviction_rate) to get the biggest ROI.

Fragmentation metrics (we will expose these):
- free_bytes_total, free_runs_count, largest_free_run, fragmentation_ratio = 1 - (largest_free_run / free_bytes_total)
- average_hole_size, relocated_bytes_per_minute, compaction_cpu_seconds
- eviction-induced-backend-fetch_rate: fraction of evicted keys that are re-requested within M seconds (default M=30s).

SLO and safety knobs:
- max_background_cpu_percent: cap on background compaction CPU usage (default 5%).
- max_reloc_time_per_slice_ms (default 4ms) to avoid introducing tail latency.
- preemption: if any foreground RPC sees latency > target*1.2, pause background compaction for 1s.
- emergency-evict-mode: when free memory < low_watermark, fall back to fastest eviction path (best-fit cold-first) until free_memory > safe_watermark. Log and alert.

Observability and rollout metrics:
- Track histograms per-arena: eviction latency, compaction slice duration, relocations_per_second, sampling_hits_per_sec, promotion_rate, demotion_rate.
- Add tracing spans: hotness-sample, tier-move, relocation(copy), eviction(decision).
- Dashboards: (1) Per-cluster fragmentation heatmap; (2) Eviction-induced miss rate trend; (3) Background CPU and pause events.

Operational playbook (quick):
- Start with sampling_rate=50 (cheap) and aggressive demotion thresholds to keep cold tier available. Run for 2 weeks in canary with synthetic bursty workload.
- If eviction-induced-backend-fetch_rate > 0.2, lower sampling_rate (make hotness more conservative) and increase demotion delay.
- For nodes showing high fragmentation_ratio and low eviction_rate, bump compaction budget gradually.

Pseudocode: eviction selection (simplified)
function select_eviction_candidate(arena, target_bytes):
    candidates = sample_free_runs(arena, k=64)
    score_list = []
    for run in candidates:
        frag_score = run.length / arena.free_bytes_total
        weight = frag_score * run.length
        score_list.append((run, weight))
    winner = weighted_random_choice(score_list)
    return winner

function should_evict(item):
    hot = get_hot_score(item.key_hash)
    prob = base_prob * exp(-beta * hot)
    return random() < prob

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Sampling rate vs. accuracy: higher sampling improves hotness detection but increases CPU overhead and metadata churn. We need realistic numbers from production traces to set defaults.
- Relocation cost model: is it better to relocate many small objects or a few large ones? The ROI depends on future allocation patterns; we should add a learning-based estimator later.
- Durability concerns when using async relocate: what invariants do we need for crash consistency in Private/On-prem deployments?

Experiment matrix (initial canary):
- A: sampling_rate=50, demote_epoch=30s, compaction_budget=64KiB/100ms (baseline)
- B: sampling_rate=20, demote_epoch=60s, compaction_budget=128KiB/100ms (aggressive compaction)
- C: sampling_rate=100, demote_epoch=15s, compaction_budget=32KiB/100ms (low CPU)
Metrics to measure: eviction-induced-backend-fetch_rate, 50/95/99th token latency delta, fragmentation_ratio change over 7 days, CPU used by reclaimer.

Migration and compatibility notes:
- Provide a shim mode where new metadata fields (tier, hot_score_mod) are stored in a small side-table to avoid changing on-disk allocations. This enables non-disruptive rollout.
- All changes should default to off; enable via per-cluster feature flag; use progressively larger canary rings.

Implementation roadmap (phases):
- Phase 0: HotnessSketch + sampling hooks in request path (low-risk; no compaction yet).
- Phase 1: Tier metadata + demotion/promotion + eviction probability adjustments (safe default: only cold evictions).
- Phase 2: Background reclaimer with relocation + rate-limits and tracing.
- Phase 3: Learning-based ROI estimator + cross-node coordination for global placement.

Appendix: small examples and operator notes:
- Example: bursty QPS doubling for 20s — expectation: hot items remain in hot/warm due to sampling; cold eviction avoids thrashing; fallback eviction probability tuned to avoid evicting newly warmed items.
- Operator escalation: if node enters emergency-evict-mode frequently, run "cache-inspect" tool to dump fragmentation metrics and recent promotion/demotion histogram; escalate to infra if relocation rate is high (>500MB/min) indicating noisy neighbor or memory leak.

Next steps:
- Instrument production traces to pick decay_factor and sampling_rate defaults.
- Build a prototype HotnessSketch and run microbenchmarks to measure overhead at QPS ranges.
- Align allocator API changes with platform team to add optional relocate() semantics.

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc leans pragmatic: small metadata changes + background work slices to reduce risk. It intentionally postpones large intrusive allocator rewrites. Feedback wanted on: sampling parameters, safety knobs, and compaction budgeting heuristics.

-- end --
